title: 12 Days in Egypt: Cairo, the Nile & the Red Sea
excerpt: A 12-day Egypt itinerary: Cairo, Abu Simbel, a three-night Nile cruise to Luxor and three Hurghada beach days. From €1,739 per person, as listed Nov 2026.
body_html:
Prices, timetables and visiting details are a November 2026 snapshot. Check the linked official pages and your departure’s current inclusions and terms before booking.

Quick answer

Twelve days is enough for Cairo, a Nile cruise and the Red Sea in one trip. The shape that works: three nights in Cairo for the pyramids, a flight to Aswan for Abu Simbel, a three-night cruise north to Luxor, a road transfer to Hurghada for three beach nights, then a short flight back to Cairo for the last night. Sawa Tours lists it as one package, Egypt End to End, from €1,739 per person, as listed in November 2026.

Check current UK government travel advice for Egypt before making your arrangements; advice can change.

Key facts

Fact Detail
Duration 12 days, 11 nights: 3 in Cairo, 1 in Aswan, 3 aboard the Nile cruise, 3 in Hurghada, then 1 more in Cairo
Route Cairo, fly to Aswan, cruise north to Luxor, road to Hurghada, fly back to Cairo
Departs (as listed in November 2026) Mondays and Saturdays from Cairo
Cost From €1,739 per person, as listed in November 2026, with hotels in three comfort tiers, the cruise, both domestic flights and Abu Simbel included
Meals included 11 breakfasts, 5 lunches, 6 dinners
Red Sea part 3 free days in Hurghada; optional shared boat trips from €31

Beach or pyramids is a false choice in Egypt: with 12 days you can have both, provided the order is right. This post walks through the 12-day Egypt itinerary: three nights in Cairo for the pyramids, Saqqara and the museum, a flight south to Aswan for Abu Simbel, a three-night Nile cruise north to Luxor, three beach days in Hurghada, then an included flight back to Cairo. Sawa Tours (sawa.tours), the Egypt shared-departure platform, lists this route as one package; its founder has worked in Egyptian tourism since 1993.

How to combine Cairo, a Nile cruise and the Red Sea in 12 days

Do the history first and the beach last. Three nights in Cairo cover the pyramids and the museum; a flight takes you to Aswan for Abu Simbel; a cruise carries you three nights north to Luxor; then a road transfer crosses the Eastern Desert to Hurghada, and a short flight returns you to Cairo. The sequence works because Luxor sits on the Nile roughly four hours by road from Hurghada, so the cruise ends close to where the beach begins.

It also keeps flying to a minimum: two domestic flights in total, Cairo to Aswan on day 4 and Hurghada to Cairo on day 11. The one long drive, roughly four hours through the Eastern Desert from Luxor to Hurghada, replaces a third flight.

The route's one rule: sightseeing first, beach last. Reverse the order and the trip's two heaviest days, Abu Simbel on arrival in Aswan and both banks of Luxor before the drive, land when you are least ready for them.

What a 12-day Egypt itinerary looks like, day by day

The table follows the Egypt End to End package as listed in November 2026: two Cairo sightseeing days, one Abu Simbel day, a three-night cruise and three free beach days. Check the package page for the exact content of your departure.

Day Base What happens
1 Cairo Arrival and first hotel night.
2 Cairo Memphis, Egypt's first capital; the tombs and Step Pyramid of Djoser at Saqqara; Old Cairo, with the Hanging Church and the Coptic district.
3 Cairo The Egyptian Museum, then the Giza plateau: the Great Pyramids, the Sphinx and the Valley Temple.
4 Aswan Fly Cairo to Aswan, then Abu Simbel by road, the temples of Ramses II and Nefertari above Lake Nasser; night in an Aswan hotel. A long day.
5 Cruise The High Dam, the Unfinished Obelisk and Philae Temple; join the cruise.
6 Cruise Sail north to Kom Ombo, the riverside double temple of Sobek the crocodile god and Horus the Elder; sail on towards Edfu.
7 Cruise The Temple of Horus at Edfu; sail north and moor in Luxor for the night.
8 Hurghada Leave the boat; West Bank: the Valley of the Kings, Hatshepsut's temple and the Colossi of Memnon; East Bank: Karnak and Luxor Temple; then the desert road to Hurghada. A very long day.
9 Hurghada Free beach day: swim, snorkel or dive, or book a boat trip.
10 Hurghada Second free day, with nothing scheduled by design.
11 Cairo Fly Hurghada to Cairo (about an hour in the air); final Cairo night.
12 Cairo Fly home.

The 11 nights split three in Cairo, one in Aswan, three aboard, three in Hurghada, and a final night back in Cairo. Meals run to 11 breakfasts, five lunches and six dinners.

Only two flights and one desert drive

Logistics are simpler than on most multi-centre trips: the package lists both domestic flights, so you never book a domestic connection yourself. The drive from Luxor to Hurghada, roughly four hours through the Eastern Desert, is the only long overland leg apart from the Abu Simbel road.

  • Day 4 is a long day. It packs the flight to Aswan, the road out to Abu Simbel (3.5 to 4 hours each way) and the temples themselves before your night in Aswan. Keep the evening free.
  • Day 8 is a very long day. It runs from leaving the boat through both banks of Luxor to about four hours on the desert road. Expect to arrive in Hurghada tired.
  • River timings flex. Lock passages and river traffic between Edfu and Luxor can shift sailing times, so treat cruise-day timings as approximate.
  • Pack a beach bag separately. A small bag with swimwear and sandals saves opening the main suitcase on arrival in Hurghada.
  • Start day 8 early. The Valley of the Kings opens at 06:00, and the tombs are coolest and emptiest in the first hours.

What the from-price covers, and what to budget separately

The from-price of €1,739 per person, as listed in November 2026, bundles most of the costs you cannot avoid: 11 hotel and cruise nights, both domestic flights, the guided sightseeing on the itinerary and Abu Simbel. What is left for you:

Included in the from-price Budget separately
11 breakfasts, 5 lunches and 6 dinners International flights to and from Cairo
4 nights in Cairo, 1 in Aswan, 3 on the cruise and 3 in Hurghada, in three comfort tiers Drinks and personal expenses
Both domestic flights: Cairo to Aswan and Hurghada to Cairo Travel insurance, which Sawa's terms require
Abu Simbel, and a licensed guide with your group for the sightseeing Tips: baksheesh, the custom of small tips for services, is a normal part of travelling in Egypt
The sightseeing listed on the package page Optional extras, and special tombs such as Tutankhamun's, which need an extra ticket

Making the most of the three Hurghada days

Hurghada's days are deliberately empty: after eight days of early starts, the empty schedule is the point. Both free days work unplanned, with the hotel pool, the marina or the promenade. If you want one day on the water, Sawa lists two shared boat trips from the resort, both about eight hours, per person as listed in November 2026:

Boat day Shape of the day From price (per person)
Dolphin House Adventure Snorkel stops and the Dolphin House bay, where wild dolphins are often seen €35
Orange Bay Escape Reef stops, then beach time on Orange Bay Island €31

Check each tour page for what is included. Dolphin sightings are common but never certain: the dolphins are wild. Both boat days are shared day-tour departures, so the same four-traveller GoAhead rule applies before anything is charged, under the day-tour terms.

Who the 12 days suit, and who should adjust

This itinerary suits first-timers, couples and solo travellers who want Egypt's headline history and a proper beach rest without planning two separate trips, and anyone who has had a group tour cancelled before, because the departure rules below mean you pay nothing until the date is confirmed. It is less right for divers who want a full Red Sea week, or for returning visitors who have already seen Giza and Karnak.

The honest costs are pace and heat: days 4 and 8 are long, and the inland sites are at their hottest from May to September, so October to April is the comfortable window. If you have only a week or so, the Egypt in Depth 9-day Nile cruise and Cairo package keeps the history and drops the beach, from €1,403 per person, as listed in November 2026.

How to do the 12 days with Sawa Tours

Sawa Tours is an Egypt shared-departure platform, operated by Online Era (registration 148500). It runs a fixed catalogue: Sawa sets the calendar and the prices, and travellers booked through several selling agencies share one tour, one date, one guide and one price, never more than eight to a group. On the cruise, your group of up to 8 sails on a shared five-star ship and does the excursions together with its guide.

Reserving a seat is free and needs no card, and nothing is charged before the GoAhead, the moment four travellers (people, not bookings) have reserved the date. You then pay a 25% deposit, and the balance is due 14 days before departure. A package date has until 30 days before departure to reach four; if it does not, it is cancelled, nothing is charged and Sawa suggests another date. A confirmed date is not cancelled for low numbers. Cancel 30 or more days before departure and there is no charge; from 29 to 15 days before, you lose half the deposit (12.5% of the price); at 14 days or fewer, or if you do not show, the deposit (25%) is retained. Some components, such as flights and cruise cabins, may become non-refundable earlier; if so, that is disclosed before you pay. Force majeure means a full refund. A traveller who does not pay after the GoAhead is excluded, and the tour still runs for everyone else. The full rules are in the terms and the GoAhead promise, and how the GoAhead works explains the mechanics.

Payments go through a secure payment link from Online Era (General Sales Agent licence 32241); charges are in euros. The departure is operated by one of the licensed Egyptian agencies with travellers on the date, named before the deposit is due. Sawa's founding operating partner is Capital Travel Service (licence 2179). Browse forming departures or see how it works, then start your own date on the package if yours is not listed; Sawa reviews it before it opens. Questions go to WhatsApp at +20 109 284 7613, answered 24/7 while your tour is running.

The verdict: should you add the Red Sea to your Egypt trip?

If you have 12 days, add the Red Sea. Three beach nights after the cruise turn a sightseeing marathon into a holiday, and the Hurghada to Cairo flight is already in the from-price. Next step: browse forming departures on Sawa, or start your own date on the Egypt End to End package. Reserving a seat is free.

tldr: Twelve days is enough for Cairo, a Nile cruise and the Red Sea in one trip. The shape that works: three nights in Cairo for the pyramids, a flight to Aswan for Abu Simbel, a three-night cruise north to Luxor, a road transfer to Hurghada for three beach nights, then a short flight back to Cairo for the last night. faq.q: Is 12 days enough for Cairo, the Nile and the Red Sea?
faq.a: Yes. The 12 days break into four nights in Cairo (three at the start, one at the end), one in Aswan, three aboard a Nile cruise and three in Hurghada. That is enough for the pyramids, the Egyptian Museum, Abu Simbel, the main Nile temples and real beach time. It is a full programme, so expect two long days.

faq.q: When is the best time of year for this itinerary?
faq.a: October to April is the comfortable window, because the sightseeing days in Luxor, Aswan and Abu Simbel are the hottest part of the trip. Summer is workable if you accept heat on the Nile and keep the Hurghada days for the water. Winter evenings on deck can be cool, so pack a layer.

faq.q: Do I need to arrange the domestic flights myself?
faq.a: No. Both domestic flights are included in the package: Cairo to Aswan on day 4, when you continue to Abu Simbel the same day, and Hurghada to Cairo on day 11. You only book your international flights into and out of Cairo.

faq.q: Can I take this trip solo without paying extra?
faq.a: The price is fixed per traveller, and Sawa's day tours have no solo surcharge. On a package with hotel nights and a cruise, solo rooms and cabins are confirmed in the booking, so check the package page or ask Sawa before you reserve. Groups are never larger than eight, so solo travellers get a small ready-made group for sightseeing.

faq.q: What happens if my departure date never fills?
faq.a: Nothing is charged until a date reaches four travellers and gets the GoAhead. If a package date has not reached four by 30 days before departure, it is cancelled, you pay nothing and Sawa suggests other dates. Once a date is confirmed it is not cancelled for low numbers.

faq.q: How much cash should I budget on top of the package?
faq.a: Set money aside for four things the from-price excludes: international flights, travel insurance, drinks and personal spending, and tips. Baksheesh, the local custom of small payments for services, is a normal part of travelling in Egypt. Optional extras, such as a Hurghada boat day from €31, are paid separately if you choose them.

faq.q: Is there a version of the trip without the beach?
faq.a: Yes. Egypt in Depth, the 9-day Nile cruise and Cairo package, keeps the Cairo days and a Nile cruise but drops Hurghada and Abu Simbel, from €1,403 per person, as listed in November 2026. It suits travellers with one week or so who want the history at a slower pace.
